title: India | RBI Customer Service, Fair Practices and Grievance Redress
tagline: Handle complaints, the Internal Ombudsman and the RBI Ombudsman, sell fairly, recover dues decently and protect customers from electronic fraud under RBI's rules.
sectors: Foreign banks operating branches in India
Card issuers and digital banking teams
Recovery agencies and direct selling agents working for banks
description:
This quest teaches the Reserve Bank of India's customer protection rules for commercial banks. It is based on the **RBI (Commercial Banks - Internal Ombudsman) Directions, 2026**, the **Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026**, the **Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025** and its 2026 amendments on mis-selling, fraudulent electronic transactions and recovery agents (all effective from 1 January 2027), the certification rule in the **Miscellaneous Directions, 2025** and the card Directions.

RBI expects banks to use complaint analysis to train frontline staff, to train card call-centre staff to handle and escalate complaints, to certify staff before posting them to third-party product sales, and to use only IIBF-certified recovery agents. The quest supports those duties for branch, contact-centre, grievance, sales, collections and digital banking staff and their managers.

In five stages you join the grievance team of a fictional Indian bank: complaints and the Internal Ombudsman, the RBI Ombudsman, fair sales, fair lending and recovery, and electronic fraud liability with inspection readiness.

The quest builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own customer service, grievance, sales and recovery policies; always follow them and the latest RBI text.
audience: Branch, contact-centre and grievance redress staff at commercial banks in India who receive and resolve complaints
Staff in the Internal Ombudsman's secretariat and the customer service and compliance functions
Relationship managers and sales staff who sell own or third-party products, and managers of DSAs and DMAs
Collections staff and managers who oversee recovery agencies
Digital banking, card and fraud operations staff who handle fraudulent electronic transaction complaints
outcomes: Classify, escalate and close complaints as the Internal Ombudsman Directions 2026 require, within the 30-day limit
Explain when and how a customer can go to the RBI Ombudsman under RB-IOS 2026, and what the bank must tell them
Apply RBI's 2027 rules on explicit consent, suitability, bundling, dark patterns and refunds for mis-selling
Confirm staff certification before posting to third-party product sales and identify regulator-prescribed qualifications
Recover dues within RBI's conduct rules for recovery agents, contact hours, call records and device locking
Decide customer liability in fraudulent electronic banking transactions and meet RBI's reversal and response timelines

quest.name: The Fair Redress Mission
quest.premise: You have just joined Deccan Lotus Bank, a fictional commercial bank headquartered in Mumbai with branches across India, as its Customer Protection Officer. A Nashik trader says she was sold insurance she never wanted, a recovery agent called her at night, and then fraudsters emptied her account. New RBI rules start on 1 January 2027. With Meera, Harpreet, Arjun and Farhan, clear five stages, then face the final boss: the RBI inspector's exam.

sessions.title: Complaints and the Internal Ombudsman: RBI's 2026 Directions
sessions.summary: Learn what RBI counts as a complaint, how a commercial bank must record, escalate and decide it within 30 days, and how the Internal Ombudsman reviews every partly resolved or rejected complaint before the customer hears no.
objectives: Define a complaint, deficiency in service and a customer as the Internal Ombudsman Directions 2026 do
Apply the three decision categories, auto-escalation and the 30-day limit to a live complaint
Describe who can be the Internal Ombudsman, to whom the IO reports and what the IO may not do
Explain how the Board's Customer Service Committee, internal audit and RBI oversee the IO framework

cards.title: Day one at Deccan Lotus Bank
cards.setting: Central Grievance Redress Cell, Deccan Lotus Bank head office, Lower Parel, Mumbai. 9:15 am.

lines.text: You have just joined Deccan Lotus Bank, a fictional commercial bank with branches across India, as its Customer Protection Officer.
Welcome! Your first file is on the screen. Sunita Patil, a textile trader in Nashik, wrote to the branch three weeks ago.
(from her letter) I asked for a working-capital loan. Somebody added an insurance policy I never asked for, and the premium came out of my loan.
The branch marked it 'closed, customer explained'. No reply went to her. Nobody escalated it.
And I never saw it. If a branch quietly rejects a complaint, my office never gets the chance to review it.
Stage one of your mission: learn how RBI wants complaints recorded, escalated and decided. Then tell me what went wrong in Nashik.

cards.title: Why RBI created the Internal Ombudsman

scenes.heading: Every complaint counts
scenes.narration: RBI treats a complaint as any representation, in writing or another mode, that alleges a deficiency in the bank's service. The customer does not have to ask for anything specific.

scenes.heading: A second look inside
scenes.narration: Before a bank tells a customer no, or only partly yes, an independent Internal Ombudsman reviews the case. That is the IO's whole job.

scenes.heading: Automatic, not optional
scenes.narration: The bank's complaint system must send every partly resolved or wholly rejected complaint to the IO automatically. Staff cannot choose to skip it.

scenes.heading: Thirty days
scenes.narration: The bank must give the customer its final decision within thirty days of receiving the complaint, including the IO's review.

scenes.heading: Then the RBI Ombudsman
scenes.narration: If the answer is still no, the bank must tell the customer how to approach the RBI Ombudsman. You will explore that route in stage two.

cards.title: A complaint's path inside the bank
cards.caption: From the Internal Ombudsman Directions 2026, paragraph 14.

items.label: Register and acknowledge
items.detail: Record it in the fully automated Complaints Management System.

items.label: Examine and decide
items.detail: Fully Resolved, Partially Resolved or Wholly Rejected: the only three categories.

items.label: Senior review
items.detail: A partly resolved or rejected case is reviewed at a fairly senior level, not closed by the same touch point.

items.label: Auto-escalate to the IO
items.detail: Within 20 days of receipt, or early enough for 10 days of IO review where RBI, NPCI or card network timelines apply.

items.label: IO's reasoned decision
items.detail: The IO records reasons and may recommend compensation.

items.label: Reply within 30 days
items.detail: Say the IO reviewed it and explain the RBI Ombudsman option.

cards.question: Sunita's letter alleges a service failure but asks for nothing specific. Is it a complaint under the IO Directions 2026?
options: No, because a complaint must state the relief the customer wants
Yes, because a representation alleging deficiency in service counts with or without a request for relief
Only if she files it on the bank's official complaint form
cards.explanation: The Directions define a complaint as a representation, in writing or through other modes, alleging deficiency in service, with or without seeking relief. The form and the request for relief do not matter.

cards.title: Who the Directions cover and the key terms
cards.body:
**Who:** commercial banks with **10 or more banking outlets in India** as on 31 March 2025, whether incorporated in India or abroad. Small finance banks, payments banks and local area banks have their own Directions. A bank that crosses the threshold later must comply six months after it qualifies.

**Key terms**
- **Complaint:** a representation in writing or another mode alleging deficiency in service, with or without a request for relief.
- **Deficiency in service:** a shortcoming in a service the bank must provide, by law or otherwise, whether or not it causes financial loss.
- **Customer:** anyone who uses, or applies for, a bank service. Sunita counts as a customer for her loan application as well as her account.
- **Competent Authority:** the whole-time director or executive director in charge of customer service.

Most provisions applied on issue (14 January 2026). The rules on the number of IOs, the three categories and senior review applied from 30 June 2026.

cards.title: Can the Internal Ombudsman take it?
cards.prompt: Sort each matter: is it within the IO's review, or outside the Directions?

items.text: A rejected complaint about a wrong charge on a savings account
A partly resolved complaint about a delayed loan statement
A service failure arising from a credit decision, such as an unanswered loan application
An employee's grievance about pay and promotion
A dispute already decided by a consumer commission
A suggestion that the bank open on Sundays
A credit report dispute with a remedy under section 18 of the CIC Act
A wholly rejected complaint about a failed card refund

cards.title: The quiet closure
cards.setting: Video call with the Nashik branch. 11:40 am.

lines.text: Your branch closed Sunita's complaint as 'customer explained'. Which of the three categories is that?
The branch manager explains that the old system had a free-text field and a 'closed' button.
Then the system is the problem. The Directions allow only Fully Resolved, Partially Resolved or Wholly Rejected.
And the same branch should never close its own rejected complaint. A senior reviewer looks first, then it goes to Harpreet automatically.
(on the line) I just want someone to tell me why money left my loan account for a policy I never signed.

cards.title: Day 19 of Sunita's complaint
cards.situation: Sunita's complaint arrived 19 days ago. The branch now proposes to refund half the premium and keep the policy running, because she signed a loan form. No RBI, NPCI or card network timeline applies. You must decide what happens next in the Complaints Management System.

choices.text: Record it as Partially Resolved, send it for senior review and let the system escalate it to the IO now
choices.outcome: Right. A partial refund is a partial resolution. It must be reviewed at a senior level and reach the IO within 20 days of receipt, leaving time for a reasoned decision before day 30.

choices.text: Record it as Fully Resolved, since the bank is giving her some money back
choices.outcome: Mislabelling a partial outcome as full avoids the IO review the Directions require. Internal audit checks auto-escalation every year and RBI supervisors review grievance handling.

choices.text: Reply to Sunita with the partial refund today and escalate to the IO only if she complains again
choices.outcome: Partly right on speed, but the IO must review partly resolved complaints before the final reply. Asking the customer to complain twice defeats the auto-escalation rule.

choices.text: Wait for the insurer's view before classifying the complaint
choices.outcome: Delay puts the 30-day limit at risk and the 20-day escalation point is tomorrow. Gather facts in parallel, but classify and escalate on time.

items.label: Board's Customer Service Committee
items.detail: Sets IO numbers and pay, approves removals, receives IO reports and reviews overruled decisions.

items.label: Competent Authority
items.detail: Whole-time or executive director for customer service; IO's administrative boss; only one who can overrule the IO.

items.label: Internal Ombudsman and Deputy IO
items.detail: Review partly resolved and rejected complaints and analyse complaint patterns.

items.label: Bank's grievance machinery
items.detail: Branches, contact centre and grievance cell that decide complaints first.

cards.title: The IO's rulebook
cards.prompt: Match each rule to what the Directions say.

pairs.right: Retired or serving GM-equivalent officer with at least seven years of relevant experience; never employed by the bank or its group
Contractual, a fixed term of at least three years, and no more than five years in total
Administratively to the Competent Authority; functionally to the Board's Customer Service Committee
Only with the Competent Authority's approval, and every such case goes to the Customer Service Committee
Not published, because the IO does not take complaints directly from customers
The IO does not represent the bank before any court or forum

cards.question: The head of retail disagrees with the IO's decision to award Sunita compensation. Who can overrule the IO?
options: The head of retail, if the business line bears the cost
The Competent Authority, with the case then placed before the Customer Service Committee
The branch manager, because the branch knows the customer best
Nobody inside the bank; only the RBI Ombudsman
cards.explanation: An IO or Deputy IO decision can be overruled only with the approval of the Competent Authority (the whole-time or executive director in charge of customer service). All overruled cases must be placed before the Board's Customer Service Committee for review.

cards.back: Commercial banks with 10 or more banking outlets in India as on 31 March 2025 must follow the IO Directions.
Default deadline to auto-escalate a partly resolved or rejected complaint to the IO, counted from receipt.
Minimum IO review time where RBI, NPCI or card network rules set a resolution timeline.
The bank must communicate its final decision within 30 days of receiving the complaint.
Time to send RBI's Consumer Education and Protection Department the details of a newly appointed IO or Deputy IO.
Quarterly IO report to RBI is due by the 15th of the month after the quarter ends.

cards.title: Real case: RBL Bank penalty (RBI, 2023)
cards.body:
**What happened.** By an order dated 6 March 2023, RBI imposed a penalty of about **₹2.27 crore** on RBL Bank Limited. The order covered RBI directions on the Internal Ombudsman Scheme 2018, the Fair Practices Code for Lenders, credit card operations, outsourcing and recovery agents.

**What RBI found.** Reviewing complaints against recovery agents, RBI found among other things that the bank had **not properly communicated its Internal Ombudsman's decision** in certain cases. Other findings concerned recovery agents, which you will meet in stage four.

**Why it matters.** The IO review only protects customers if its outcome actually reaches them. Today's Directions spell this out: the reply must say the IO reviewed the case and must explain the RBI Ombudsman option.

RBI said the penalty addressed regulatory compliance and did not rule on the validity of any customer transaction.

*Source: RBI press release 2022-2023/1891.*

cards.title: Write the reply the IO rules expect
cards.body:
When the IO upholds a rejection or partial resolution, the reply to the customer should:

- Say clearly that the **Internal Ombudsman has reviewed** the complaint.
- Give the **reasons**, matching the IO's reasoned decision.
- Explain the option of going to the **RBI Ombudsman**, with the CMS portal address (cms.rbi.org.in) and the CRPC's postal and email address.
- Reach the customer **within 30 days** of the bank receiving the complaint.

Never put the IO's own contact details in the reply. The IO does not take complaints directly.

cards.title: Grievance Desk take-aways
items: A complaint is any representation alleging deficiency in service, with or without a request for relief.
Use only three outcomes: Fully Resolved, Partially Resolved or Wholly Rejected. Partly resolved and rejected cases go to the IO automatically.
Escalate within 20 days by default, give the IO at least 10 days where external timelines apply, and reply within 30 days.
The IO is independent: never employed by the bank, on a fixed contract, and can be overruled only by the Competent Authority.
The Customer Service Committee, annual internal audit and RBI supervision all oversee the framework.

cards.prompt: Think about how complaints reach your team. Where could a partly resolved or rejected complaint get closed without senior review or escalation? What would you change first?

quiz.question: Which commercial banks must follow the RBI (Commercial Banks - Internal Ombudsman) Directions, 2026?
options: Every commercial bank licensed in India, whatever its size
Only banks incorporated in India with 100 or more branches
Commercial banks with 10 or more banking outlets in India as on 31 March 2025
Only public sector banks and the State Bank of India
quiz.explanation: The Directions apply to commercial banks with 10 or more banking outlets in India as on 31 March 2025, whether incorporated in India or abroad. Small finance, payments and local area banks have separate Directions.

quiz.question: A customer emails the branch saying her cheque book request was ignored for six weeks. She does not ask for compensation. How should the bank treat the email?
options: As a query, because no relief is sought
As a complaint, since it alleges a deficiency in service
As feedback for the branch manager only
As a complaint only once she uses the bank's form
quiz.explanation: A complaint is a representation in writing or other modes alleging deficiency in service, with or without seeking relief. Asking for nothing does not turn it into a query.

quiz.question: Which set of decision categories may a bank's Complaints Management System offer before a complaint goes to the Internal Ombudsman?
options: Fully Resolved, Partially Resolved and Wholly Rejected
Resolved, Closed and Referred
Accepted, Rejected and Withdrawn by customer
Closed with explanation, Refunded and Pending
quiz.explanation: The Directions allow only three categories: Fully Resolved, Partially Resolved and Wholly Rejected. Partly resolved and rejected complaints are then auto-escalated to the IO.

quiz.question: A debit card complaint falls under a resolution timeline set by a card network. When must the bank escalate it to the IO if it plans to reject it?
options: Early enough that the IO has at least 10 days to review it within the external timeline
Within 20 days of receipt, whatever the network timeline
Only after the network timeline has expired
Within 30 days, at the same time as the final reply
quiz.explanation: Where RBI, NPCI or card network guidelines set a timeline, escalation must be early enough to give the IO at least 10 days. The 20-day rule applies only to other complaints.

quiz.question: Ravi complained to Deccan Lotus Bank on 1 March about a wrong charge. No external timeline applies. By when must the bank communicate its final decision?
options: Within 30 days of the bank receiving the complaint
Within 45 days of the complaint
Within 20 days of the complaint
Within 30 days of the Internal Ombudsman's decision
quiz.explanation: The bank must communicate the final decision within 30 days of receiving the complaint. Twenty days is the default escalation point to the IO, not the reply deadline.

quiz.question: Which person could be appointed as Deccan Lotus Bank's Internal Ombudsman?
options: Deccan Lotus Bank's own retired head of retail banking
A serving GM of another bank who keeps that job part-time
A retired GM-rank officer of another bank with eight years of relevant experience
A 69-year-old former regulator appointed for a three-year term
quiz.explanation: The IO must be a retired or serving GM-equivalent officer with at least seven years' relevant experience, must never have worked for the bank or its group, must give up any serving post, and must not pass 70 before the tenure ends.

quiz.question: To whom does the Internal Ombudsman report?
options: Administratively and functionally to the Chief Compliance Officer
Administratively to the Competent Authority and functionally to the Board's Customer Service Committee
To the head of retail banking for both purposes
Directly to RBI's Consumer Education and Protection Department
quiz.explanation: The IO reports administratively to the Competent Authority (the whole-time or executive director in charge of customer service) and functionally to the Customer Service Committee of the Board.

quiz.question: A customer writes directly to the Internal Ombudsman's office about a new problem with her account. What should happen?
options: The IO decides it at once to save time
The IO forwards it to RBI's Ombudsman
The IO rejects it and closes the matter
The bank's grievance machinery handles it first, since the IO reviews only complaints already examined by the bank
quiz.explanation: The IO office does not handle complaints received directly from complainants. It deals only with complaints the bank has examined and partly resolved or rejected.

quiz.question: Which matter is outside the Internal Ombudsman's purview under the 2026 Directions?
options: A complaint already pending before a consumer disputes commission
A rejected complaint about a delayed pension credit
A partly resolved complaint about wrong loan interest
A service lapse linked to a commercial decision of the bank
quiz.explanation: Matters decided by or pending before courts, consumer commissions or arbitration are excluded. Service deficiencies within commercial decisions remain valid complaints for the IO.

quiz.question: What must internal audit cover in its annual audit of the IO Directions?
options: Whether each IO decision was correct on the merits
Only the number of complaints the IO decided
The IO's personal performance rating for the Board
Appointment process, IO resources, timely auto-escalation and reporting, but not whether IO decisions were correct
quiz.explanation: The annual audit covers appointment, resources, auto-escalation within timelines, analysis, staff awareness and reporting to RBI. It expressly excludes assessing the correctness of IO decisions.

sessions.title: Beyond the Bank: the RBI Ombudsman under RB-IOS 2026
sessions.summary: Follow a complaint out of the bank to the RBI Ombudsman: who is covered by the Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2026, when a customer can file, which complaints are not maintainable, how settlement, awards and appeals work, and what the bank must do.
objectives: Explain what RB-IOS 2026 is, when it took effect and which banks it covers
Apply the 30-day and 90-day filing windows and the main non-maintainability grounds
Describe settlement, awards, compensation limits and appeals under the Scheme
State what the bank must tell customers and send to the RBI Ombudsman

cards.title: Sunita goes to RBI
cards.setting: Central Grievance Redress Cell, Mumbai. Thursday, 4:00 pm.

lines.text: Harpreet reviewed Sunita's complaint. She ordered a full premium refund, but the policy question is still disputed with the insurer.
(on the phone) My nephew says I can go to the RBI Ombudsman. Do I need a lawyer? Do I have to travel to Mumbai?
Our reply must explain that route clearly. If she files, the bank must also send my decision to the RBI Ombudsman.
Stage two: learn the RBI Ombudsman route well enough to answer Sunita honestly, without discouraging her.

scenes.heading: Free and non-adversarial
scenes.narration: The Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2026 is RBI's cost-free, quick and non-adversarial alternate route for complaints about deficiency in service.

scenes.heading: New since July 2026
scenes.narration: It came into force on the first of July 2026 and replaced the 2021 Scheme. Complaints received before that date stay under the 2021 Scheme.

scenes.heading: One Nation One Ombudsman
scenes.narration: Complaints are handled jurisdiction-neutrally. A customer does not need to approach a particular Ombudsman office; RBI allocates the case.

scenes.heading: Three ways to file
scenes.narration: Online on the CMS portal at cms dot rbi dot org dot in, by email to the CRPC, or by post to the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre in Chandigarh.

scenes.heading: Settle, award or reject
scenes.narration: The Ombudsman first tries to settle. If that fails and there is a deficiency, it can pass an award. Only awards can be appealed.

cards.title: When Sunita can file
cards.caption: Based on RBI's RB-IOS 2026 FAQs. The higher of 30 days or any RBI, NPCI or card network timeline applies.

items.label: Complaint to the bank
items.detail: She must approach the bank first and keep proof of it.

items.label: Bank's reply or silence
items.detail: She can file if no reply by then, or earlier if she gets a reply and is unhappy with it.

items.label: Filing window closes
items.detail: Within 90 days from the expiry of that timeline or the bank's last communication, whichever is later.

items.label: Award accepted
items.detail: If an award is passed, she sends an acceptance letter to the bank within 30 days, unless she appeals.

cards.question: Sunita got the bank's reply on day 22 and disagrees with it. When can she approach the RBI Ombudsman?
options: Only after day 30, whatever the bank said
Now, because she has received a reply and is not satisfied
Only after the Internal Ombudsman has met her in person
cards.explanation: A customer can file once the bank has replied and she is dissatisfied, or if there is no reply within 30 days (or the higher RBI, NPCI or card network timeline).

cards.title: Who is covered and what it costs
cards.body:
**Covered entities (RBI's FAQ, Q13)**
- **Banks:** all commercial banks, regional rural banks, state and central co-operative banks, scheduled urban co-operative banks, and non-scheduled urban co-operative banks with deposits of ₹50 crore or more.
- **NBFCs** that take deposits or have customer interface and assets of ₹100 crore or more, with listed exclusions.
- Non-bank prepaid payment instrument issuers and credit information companies.

**Cost:** nothing. No fee for filing or resolving, and no need to pay any agent.

**Representation:** a customer may use an authorised representative, but not an advocate unless the advocate is the aggrieved person.

**Language:** the CMS portal accepts Hindi and English, and the description may be in any language. Email and paper complaints may be in any language.

**Help line:** RBI's Contact Centre (14448) guides customers but cannot take complaints.

cards.title: Maintainable or not?
cards.prompt: Sort each complaint under RB-IOS 2026, using RBI's FAQ list of non-maintainable complaints.

items.text: Customer complained to the bank 40 days ago and got no reply
Customer got a rejection last week and files through her son as authorised representative
Customer never complained to the bank first
Customer files 200 days after the bank's last reply
Same grievance is already pending in a civil court
Complaint challenges the bank's commercial decision to decline a loan, with no service lapse
Customer emails her bank and only copies RBI
Police are investigating the fraud, and she complains to the Ombudsman about the bank's handling

lines.text: The branch officer told me the RBI Ombudsman takes years and that I would need a lawyer. Is that true?
No, and I apologise. The Scheme is free, and an advocate cannot represent you unless they are the aggrieved person. You can file online yourself.
Discouraging a customer from the Ombudsman is exactly the behaviour our complaint analysis should catch and feed into frontline training.
Let's turn this into a training case for the branches next month.

cards.title: Replying to the RBI Ombudsman
cards.situation: Sunita has filed on the CMS portal. The RBI Ombudsman forwards her complaint to Deccan Lotus Bank for its response. A second complaint from another customer, Mr Joseph D'Souza in Goa, also arrives from the Ombudsman; the bank never escalated his case to the IO because the branch had marked it 'resolved'.

choices.text: Send Harpreet's reasoned decision with Sunita's file, and get Harpreet's comments on Mr D'Souza's case before replying
choices.outcome: Correct. The IO's decision must be included where the IO reviewed the complaint. Where the IO did not, the bank must seek the IO's comments and submit them.

choices.text: Reply on both cases from the legal department without involving the IO
choices.outcome: This breaks paragraph 14(13): the IO decision or IO comments must form part of the bank's submission to the RBI Ombudsman.

choices.text: Send the IO decision for Sunita, and for Mr D'Souza explain that the branch had resolved it
choices.outcome: Half right. For a complaint the IO never saw, the bank must seek the IO's comments. The mislabelled case also needs internal review.

cards.title: How the RBI Ombudsman deals with a complaint

items.label: Maintainability check
items.detail: Non-maintainable complaints are closed with a reason.

items.label: Forwarded to the bank
items.detail: The bank responds, with the IO's decision or comments.

items.label: Settlement
items.detail: Facilitation, advisory or conciliation, in person or online.

items.label: Award or rejection
items.detail: Award if deficiency is found and no settlement; rejection with reasons otherwise.

items.label: Appeal on awards only
items.detail: To the Appellate Authority within 30 days.

cards.title: From award to compliance
cards.prompt: Put the steps after an RBI Ombudsman award in the right order.
steps: The RBI Ombudsman passes an award against the bank after hearing both sides
The complainant receives a copy of the award
Within 30 days, the complainant sends the bank a letter accepting the award in full and final settlement
Within 30 days of that letter, the bank complies and informs the Ombudsman, or appeals where permitted

cards.question: The RBI Ombudsman rejected a complaint because it found no deficiency in service. Can the customer appeal to the Appellate Authority under RB-IOS 2026?
options: Yes, any decision can be appealed within 30 days
No, under the 2026 Scheme an appeal lies only against an award
Yes, but only with the bank's consent
cards.explanation: RBI's FAQ (Q31) says that under RB-IOS 2026 an appeal is available only against an award passed by the RBI Ombudsman.

items.label: Filing fee
items.detail: The Scheme is cost-free for customers.

items.label: Consequential loss
items.detail: Maximum compensation for consequential loss; no cap on the amount in dispute.

items.label: Time, expense, harassment
items.detail: Extra compensation the Ombudsman may award.

items.label: Appeal window
items.detail: For a complainant, from receipt of the award; up to 30 more days for sufficient cause.

cards.back: RBI's Complaint Management System portal (cms.rbi.org.in), used to file and track complaints online.
Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre in Chandigarh; receives email and paper complaints.
RBI's Alternate Grievance Redress set-up: Ombudsman offices, CRPC, Consumer Education and Protection Cells and CEPD.
A direction to the bank to act and/or pay compensation, passed when there is a deficiency and no settlement.
Hears appeals against awards; may dismiss, allow, remand or modify.
Guidance and status help; it cannot register complaints.

cards.title: Never discourage the Ombudsman route
cards.body:
Frontline staff sometimes try to talk customers out of escalating. Don't.

- Explain the route accurately: free, online or by post, no lawyer needed.
- Give the CMS portal address and the CRPC details, as the IO Directions require in rejection or partial-resolution replies.
- Respond to RBI's forwarded complaints fully and on time. An award can follow if the bank fails to give information.
- Treat every Ombudsman case as a lesson. Complaints the RBI Ombudsman decides in the customer's favour go to the Customer Service Committee every quarter.

cards.title: Chandigarh Gate take-aways
items: RB-IOS 2026 took effect on 1 July 2026, replacing the 2021 Scheme; it is free and covers all commercial banks.
Customers must go to the bank first, then may file after 30 days (or the higher external timeline) or after an unsatisfactory reply, within 90 days.
Commercial judgments, matters before courts and complaints never raised with the bank are among those not maintainable.
The Ombudsman settles where it can; awards may include up to ₹30 lakh for consequential loss plus up to ₹3 lakh for time, expense and harassment.
Only awards can be appealed, and the bank must include the IO's decision or comments in its response.

cards.prompt: If a customer asked you tomorrow how to go to the RBI Ombudsman, could you explain it in under a minute? Write down the three things you would say.

quiz.question: When did the Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026 come into force?
options: 16 January 2026
1 July 2026
1 January 2027
28 November 2025
quiz.explanation: RBI issued the Scheme on 16 January 2026 and it came into force on 1 July 2026, replacing RB-IOS 2021. Complaints received before 1 July 2026 stay under the 2021 Scheme.

quiz.question: A customer complained to her bank on 1 August 2026 and has heard nothing. No external timeline applies. From when can she file with the RBI Ombudsman?
options: Immediately, on the day she complained
After 30 days pass without a reply
Only after 60 days without a reply
Only after the bank formally rejects it
quiz.explanation: Under RB-IOS 2026 she can file if there is no reply within 30 days (or the higher RBI, NPCI or card network timeline), or earlier if she gets an unsatisfactory reply.

quiz.question: The bank's last letter to a customer was dated 10 April. Which limit applies to his RBI Ombudsman complaint?
options: Within one year from the original transaction
Within 30 days of the bank's last letter
Within 90 days from the later of the expiry of the bank's timeline or the bank's last communication
There is no time limit once the bank has replied
quiz.explanation: RBI's FAQ says the complaint must be made within 90 days from the date the applicable timeline expires or the date of the bank's last communication, whichever is later.

quiz.question: Which complaint is NOT maintainable under RB-IOS 2026?
options: A grievance against named senior executives of the bank
A complaint about an unexplained account charge
A complaint filed by a customer's authorised daughter
A complaint where police are investigating the related fraud
quiz.explanation: Grievances against the management or executives of a regulated entity are not maintainable. A police investigation is not treated as the same grievance, and authorised representatives are allowed.

quiz.question: A customer wants an advocate he has hired to file his RBI Ombudsman complaint. What does the Scheme allow?
options: Any advocate may file on his behalf
He must always file in person at an Ombudsman office
He may use an authorised representative, but not an advocate unless the advocate is the aggrieved person
Only a chartered accountant may represent him
quiz.explanation: RB-IOS 2026 allows an authorised representative but excludes advocates unless the advocate is the aggrieved person.

quiz.question: What compensation can the RBI Ombudsman award for consequential loss under RB-IOS 2026?
options: Up to ₹30 lakh, plus up to ₹3 lakh for time, expenses and harassment
Up to ₹20 lakh, with nothing extra for harassment
Up to ₹10 lakh in total for all heads of loss
Up to ₹1 crore, depending on the bank's size
quiz.explanation: RBI's FAQ (Q22-23): there is no limit on the disputed amount, but consequential loss compensation is capped at ₹30 lakh, with up to ₹3 lakh more for time, expenses and harassment or mental anguish.

quiz.question: Which channel can a customer NOT use to lodge an RB-IOS 2026 complaint?
options: The CMS portal at cms.rbi.org.in
A call to RBI's Contact Centre on 14448
Email to crpc@rbi.org.in
A signed letter posted to the CRPC in Chandigarh
quiz.explanation: The Contact Centre guides customers and gives status updates but cannot register complaints. Complaints go through CMS, email to the CRPC, or post.

quiz.question: When Deccan Lotus Bank responds to an RBI Ombudsman complaint that its IO never reviewed, what must it do?
options: Seek the IO's comments and submit them to the RBI Ombudsman
Submit only the branch's original reply
Ask the RBI Ombudsman to send the case to the IO
Reopen the complaint internally and ask the customer to withdraw
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 14(13) of the IO Directions: include the IO's decision if the IO reviewed the complaint; if not, the bank must seek the IO's comments and submit them.

quiz.question: A customer is unhappy that the RBI Ombudsman rejected his complaint as not maintainable. What further recourse does RB-IOS 2026 itself provide?
options: An appeal to the Appellate Authority within 30 days
None within the Scheme, as appeals lie only against awards
A review by the bank's Internal Ombudsman
A fresh complaint to a different Ombudsman office
quiz.explanation: Under RB-IOS 2026, an appeal is available only against an award. Re-filing the same grievance is also non-maintainable.

quiz.question: An award goes against Deccan Lotus Bank and the customer sends a letter accepting it. What must the bank do?
options: Comply within 90 days of the award
Wait for the customer to file a fresh complaint
Appeal in every case, since appeal is automatic
Comply and inform the Ombudsman, or appeal where permitted, within 30 days of the acceptance letter
quiz.explanation: RBI's FAQ (Q29): the bank must comply with the award and inform the Ombudsman, or appeal where allowed, within 30 days of receiving the complainant's acceptance letter.

sessions.title: Fair Sales: Mis-selling, Third-Party Products and Certification
sessions.summary: Prepare for RBI's comprehensive sales rules that start on 1 January 2027: what counts as mis-selling, explicit consent, suitability, bundling, dark patterns, DSAs and refunds, plus the certification staff need before they sell third-party products.
objectives: Identify the five forms of mis-selling in the Responsible Business Conduct Second Amendment Directions
Apply the rules on explicit consent, suitability, compulsory bundling and loan-funded purchases
Spot dark patterns in digital sales journeys and explain the duties for DSAs, DMAs and third-party representatives
Explain the certification required before posting staff to third-party product sales and the refund rule for proven mis-selling

cards.title: How the policy got there
cards.setting: Regional sales office, Connaught Place, New Delhi. Monday, 10:00 am.

lines.text: My team hit 140 percent of the insurance target last quarter. The Nashik branch was our star.
One of those policies went to Sunita Patil. The premium was debited from her working-capital loan. She says nobody asked her.
It was on page four of the loan form. She signed the form.
A signature on a combined form is not the same as explicit consent for each product. From January, RBI says so in plain terms.
Stage three: rebuild our sales practices before 1 January 2027, starting with the definition of mis-selling.

scenes.heading: Not suitable
scenes.narration: Selling a product that is neither suitable nor appropriate for the customer's profile is mis-selling, even if the customer gave explicit consent.

scenes.heading: Wrong or missing information
scenes.narration: Selling without correct and complete information, or with misleading information, is mis-selling.

scenes.heading: No explicit consent
scenes.narration: Selling a product without the customer's explicit consent is mis-selling. Explicit means specific, informed, unambiguous and recorded.

scenes.heading: Compulsory bundling
scenes.narration: Making one product conditional on buying another, own or third-party, is mis-selling.

scenes.heading: Other regulators' tests
scenes.narration: Anything the relevant financial regulator, such as SEBI or the insurance regulator, defines as mis-selling also counts.

items.label: Consent
items.left: One signature on a multi-product form
items.right: Explicit consent for each product; default choice is 'No'

items.label: Fit
items.right: Suitability and appropriateness checked against the customer profile

items.label: Bundling
items.left: Loan approved if insurance bought from us
items.right: No compulsory bundling; a required risk cover can be bought from any provider

items.label: Funding
items.right: No funding of a purchase from a loan without explicit consent

items.label: Redress
items.right: Full refund where mis-selling is established, plus compensation

cards.question: A customer explicitly consents to a complex market-linked insurance plan that is unsuitable for her age and risk tolerance. Under the 2027 rules, is it mis-selling?
options: No, because she gave explicit consent
Yes, because unsuitable sales are mis-selling despite explicit consent
Only if the insurer later rejects a claim
cards.explanation: The definition covers the sale of a product that is neither suitable nor appropriate for the customer's profile, notwithstanding her explicit consent.

cards.title: Consent, disclosure and documents
cards.body:
From **1 January 2027** (paragraphs 85G-85T):

- **Explicit consent** may be a signed declaration, an OTP approval, a recorded confirmation or a clearly separate section of the agreement. On a multi-product form, list each product and let the customer choose only what she wants.
- **Keep consent records** until one year after the contract ends.
- **Disclose key features prominently**: fees, interest rate, risks, commitments, lock-in and exit penalties. Use RBI's or another regulator's format where one exists, such as the KFS or MITC.
- **Digital journeys:** the customer must go through the terms before consenting, and the default must be 'No' or 'I do not agree'.
- Use a **specific application form** for each product, showing its nature (loan, deposit, insurance, mutual fund, etc.).
- Provide documents in the regional language or one the customer understands, **acknowledge** each application, and give a **copy of the signed terms** after the sale.

cards.title: Allowed or bundling?
cards.prompt: Sort each practice under the 2027 rules on compulsory bundling.

items.text: Home loan requires property insurance as a risk mitigant, and the customer may buy it from any insurer
A free accident cover included with a card at no extra cost to the customer
A package of account, card and locker that the customer chooses voluntarily
Car loan approved only if the customer buys the bank's partner insurer's policy
Insurance premium added to the loan amount without the customer's explicit consent
Fixed deposit opened only if the customer also takes a mutual fund

cards.title: The incentive question
cards.setting: Video call between Delhi and Mumbai. 3:00 pm.

lines.text: The insurer pays my top sellers a travel bonus. It's their money, not the bank's.
From January, no bank employee may receive any incentive, directly or indirectly, from a third-party product provider.
And our own pay structures must not create incentives for mis-selling. My complaint analysis shows the spikes follow the contests.
Then I need a new scorecard, and I need it before the new year.

cards.title: The pre-approved loan pop-up
cards.situation: The digital team shows Arjun a new mobile app journey for pre-approved personal loans. A countdown timer says the rate rises in 10 minutes. A loan protection insurance box is ticked by default. Closing the pop-up after login opens the loan page anyway. Launch is planned for 15 January 2027.

choices.text: Stop the launch, remove the timer, the pre-ticked box and the forced pop-up, and send the journey for user testing and internal audit
choices.outcome: Right. These match RBI's illustrative dark patterns: false urgency, basket sneaking and forced action. User interfaces must be user-tested and audited periodically for dark patterns.

choices.text: Keep the timer but untick the insurance box
choices.outcome: Better, but a countdown suggesting the rate will rise is RBI's own example of false urgency, and the forced pop-up remains.

choices.text: Launch as designed, since customers can still read the terms
choices.outcome: From 1 January 2027 the bank and its DSAs must not deploy dark patterns at all. Disclosure elsewhere does not cure a manipulative design.

cards.title: Name the dark pattern
cards.prompt: Match each design to the dark pattern in RBI's illustrative list (Annex IIA).

pairs.right: 'Offer ends soon' timers or warnings that rates will rise to rush a decision
Fraud or loan protection cover added by default to an application
Opt-out button reading 'No, I don't want extra security for my account'
Advertising a low loan rate, then charging a higher one at application
Easy sign-up for a card, but cancellation hidden behind many steps
'Uncheck this box if you do not want to receive offers'

cards.title: Who may sell, and how they must behave
cards.caption: Paragraphs 85B-85O of the Second Amendment, and paragraphs 59-60 of the Miscellaneous Directions.

items.label: Certify before posting
items.detail: A certificate course is mandatory before staff are posted to third-party retail and wealth product sales.

items.label: Meet other regulators' rules
items.detail: Staff and DSA sub-agents must hold any qualification SEBI, IRDAI or PFRDA prescribe.

items.label: Sign the code of conduct
items.detail: Employees, DSAs, DMAs, sub-agents and third-party representatives give an undertaking.

items.label: Be identifiable
items.detail: Agents and third-party staff in a branch wear clear identification distinct from bank staff.

items.label: Contact properly
items.detail: Calls and visits normally 09:00-19:00, home visits only with explicit consent, no coercion.

cards.question: Deccan Lotus Bank wants to post a new officer to its wealth management desk to sell third-party mutual funds next week. What must happen first?
options: Nothing, provided a certified colleague supervises her
She must complete the required certificate course, including the certification SEBI prescribes for mutual fund sales
She must pass the bank's internal product quiz only
cards.explanation: Paragraph 59 of the Miscellaneous Directions makes a certificate mandatory before posting staff to marketing of third-party retail products and wealth management, and certifications prescribed by other regulators must be met. For mutual funds, SEBI requires NISM certification.

cards.back: Third-party product or service: offered by the bank for another provider under an agency or referral arrangement. Never advertise it as the bank's own.
Anyone other than a bank employee engaged to sell or promote products, whatever the contract calls them, including BCs and loan service providers.
A specific, informed and unambiguous choice, recorded through a statement or clear affirmative action.
Within 30 days of a sale, by a unit not involved in selling; findings reported every six months.
Within the timeline set by the product's regulator, otherwise within 30 days of receiving the signed terms.
If mis-selling is established: refund the full amount paid, tell the customer about cancellation, and compensate any loss under the bank's policy.

cards.title: Real case: HDFC Bank penalty (RBI, 2024)
cards.body:
**What happened.** By an order dated 3 September 2024, RBI imposed a penalty of **₹1 crore** on HDFC Bank Limited. The order covered RBI directions on interest rates on deposits, recovery agents, customer service in banks read with the BCSBI Code, and outsourcing.

**What RBI found.** Among the sustained charges, the bank had:
- **paid the first-year premium for a complimentary life insurance cover** as a gift costing more than ₹250 to depositors when accepting certain deposits;
- opened certain savings accounts for ineligible entities; and
- **failed to ensure customers were not contacted after 7 pm and before 7 am.**

**Lessons.** Tying insurance benefits to deposits and contacting customers at odd hours are conduct risks RBI inspects. The 2027 sales rules make both areas stricter.

*Source: RBI press release 2024-2025/1075.*

cards.title: Sales Floor take-aways
items: From 1 January 2027 mis-selling covers unsuitable sales, wrong or incomplete information, no explicit consent, compulsory bundling and other regulators' definitions.
Get explicit consent for each product, with 'No' as the default, and keep the records until one year after the contract ends.
No compulsory bundling, no loan-funded purchases without explicit consent, no dark patterns and no third-party incentives to staff.
Certify staff before posting them to third-party or wealth sales, and meet SEBI, IRDAI or PFRDA qualifications.
Where mis-selling is established, refund the full amount paid and compensate any loss under the bank's policy.

cards.prompt: Look at one sales journey you use or approve. Where is consent recorded for each product, and is 'No' really the default? What would you fix before 1 January 2027?

quiz.question: From when do the Responsible Business Conduct Second Amendment Directions on advertising, marketing and sale apply?
options: 15 June 2026
1 July 2026
1 January 2027
1 April 2027
quiz.explanation: The Second Amendment Directions were issued on 15 June 2026 and come into effect from 1 January 2027.

quiz.question: Which practice is defined as compulsory bundling?
options: Offering a free cover with a card at no extra cost
A package of products the customer chooses voluntarily
Approving a loan only if the customer buys another product the bank offers
Requiring property insurance that may be bought from any insurer
quiz.explanation: Compulsory bundling makes one product conditional on buying another offered by the bank. Voluntary packages, complimentary covers and a required risk cover bought from any provider are not bundling.

quiz.question: An RM sells a customer a product after giving her an incomplete picture of the lock-in and exit penalties. She signed every page. Is this mis-selling under the 2027 rules?
options: No, because she signed every page of the form
No, unless she suffers a financial loss
Yes, because selling without correct and complete information is mis-selling
Only if the product is a third-party product
quiz.explanation: Sale without correct or complete information is one of the five forms of mis-selling, whatever the customer signed, and it applies to own and third-party products.

quiz.question: In a digital consent journey, what must the default choice be under the 2027 rules?
options: 'Yes', provided the customer can change it
Whatever the product team prefers
Blank, with a pop-up suggesting 'Yes'
'No' or 'I do not agree'
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 85I requires the default consent choice to be 'No' / 'I do not agree', and the customer must go through the terms before consenting.

quiz.question: Mis-selling of a third-party insurance product is established. The customer paid ₹48,000 in premiums. What must Deccan Lotus Bank do?
options: Refund the unexpired part of the premium only
Ask the insurer to decide whether a refund is due
Refund the full ₹48,000, inform her of cancellation, and compensate any loss under its policy
Offer a different policy with the same insurer
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 85Z: where mis-selling is established, the bank refunds the entire amount paid, tells the customer about cancellation, and compensates any loss under its approved policy.

quiz.question: Before posting staff to marketing of third-party retail products, what does paragraph 59 of the Miscellaneous Directions require?
options: A three-month apprenticeship with a senior RM
A mandatory certificate course, plus any certification other financial regulators prescribe
An annual refresher only, after the first year
Approval from the Internal Ombudsman
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 59 makes acquiring a certificate course mandatory before posting staff to third-party retail and wealth sales, and certifications other regulators prescribe must also be met.

quiz.question: An insurer offers Deccan Lotus Bank's branch staff gift vouchers for every policy sold. What do the 2027 rules say?
options: No bank employee may directly or indirectly receive incentives from a third-party product provider
Vouchers are allowed below a set value
Allowed if the bank discloses them on its website
Allowed if the branch manager approves them
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 85U requires that no incentive is directly or indirectly received by bank employees from the third-party provider, and bank policies must not create incentives for mis-selling.

quiz.question: Within what time must a bank seek post-sale feedback to check customers understood a product and its risks?
options: Within 7 days, through the selling RM
Within 90 days, by the insurer
Within 30 days of the sale, through a unit not associated with sales
Within one year, at annual review
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 85Y requires a feedback mechanism within 30 days of sale, which may use random call-backs or surveys by a unit not involved in selling, with a half-yearly report.

quiz.question: A DSA sub-agent sits in a branch selling the bank's credit cards. Which requirement applies?
options: She must be clearly identifiable as distinct from bank employees and must sign up to the bank's code of conduct
She may wear the bank's uniform to build trust
She may call customers at any hour they answer
She is outside RBI rules as she is not an employee
quiz.explanation: Paragraphs 85E-85F: DSA sub-agents in branches must be distinguishable from bank employees with clear identification, and the bank must obtain undertakings that they follow its code of conduct.

quiz.question: A mobile app shows 'No thanks, I don't want extra security' as the opt-out from a fraud cover. Which dark pattern is this?
options: Confirm shaming
Drip pricing
Nagging
Disguised advertisement
quiz.explanation: Confirm shaming uses guilt or fear to push a choice. RBI's Annex IIA gives this very wording as an illustration.

sessions.title: Fair Lending, Digital Channels and Recovery Conduct
sessions.summary: Lend and collect fairly: the principles behind RBI's responsible lending conduct and digital lending rules, then the detailed recovery rules from 1 January 2027, covering IIBF-certified agents, notice, contact hours, call records, harsh practices, device locking and recovery grievances.
objectives: Explain the fair practices principles that run through RBI's responsible lending conduct rules, including for digital lending
Apply the 2027 rules on recovery policy, agency due diligence, IIBF certification and the code of conduct
Conduct or supervise recovery contacts within RBI's hours, notice, recording and decency rules
Apply the conditions and safeguards for locking a financed mobile device

cards.title: The 9:40 pm call
cards.setting: Collections hub, Gachibowli, Hyderabad. Tuesday, 9:00 am.

lines.text: (voice note) A man called me at 9:40 at night about my loan instalment. He said he would tell my suppliers I am a defaulter.
That call came from an agency we hired in August. I don't even know if the caller is certified.
Sunita missed one instalment because the insurance debit drained her loan account. Our own mis-sale caused this default.
Then this is a recovery complaint and a mis-selling complaint at once. Both feed my quarterly analysis.
Stage four: learn how RBI expects us to lend and collect, especially under the new rules from 1 January 2027.

scenes.heading: Clear terms
scenes.narration: RBI's responsible lending conduct rules, now in Chapter Eight of the Responsible Business Conduct Directions, expect borrowers to understand the cost, terms and consequences before they sign.

scenes.heading: Prescribed formats
scenes.narration: Where RBI prescribes a disclosure format, such as a Key Facts Statement, the bank must use it when it obtains consent.

scenes.heading: Digital is still the bank
scenes.narration: Loan service providers and apps that sell for the bank count as its direct selling agents, whatever the contract calls them. Their screens must avoid dark patterns.

scenes.heading: Decent recovery
scenes.narration: A borrower in default keeps the right to be treated with dignity. The 2027 rules set out exactly what decency means in recovery.

cards.title: Engaging a recovery agency from 2027
cards.caption: Section L of the Responsible Business Conduct Directions, inserted by the Fourth Amendment (6 August 2026).

items.label: Recovery policy in place
items.detail: Triggers, escalation matrix, code of conduct, deceased borrowers, financial distress and compensation.

items.label: Due diligence
items.detail: Under the outsourcing Directions; verify agents' antecedents before engagement and periodically.

items.label: IIBF certificate
items.detail: Agencies may use only agents certified by IIBF after its Debt Recovery Agents training.

items.label: Code of conduct undertaking
items.detail: The agency undertakes that its agents will follow the bank's code.

items.label: Publish the list
items.detail: Agency list on the website, updated within seven calendar days of any change.

items.label: Notify the borrower
items.detail: Agency details at least one day before the first in-person visit.

cards.question: Farhan's new agency wants to deploy a field agent who has years of experience but no IIBF certificate. What does the 2027 rule say?
options: Experience of more than five years can substitute for the certificate
The agency may engage only agents who hold the IIBF Debt Recovery Agents certificate
The bank may allow it for six months while the agent studies
cards.explanation: Paragraph 454I: the bank must ensure the agency engages only agents who have the IIBF certificate after completing the Debt Recovery Agents training from IIBF or an institute tied up with it.

cards.title: Contact rules for employees and agents
cards.body:
From **1 January 2027** (paragraphs 454P and 454X-454Y), anyone collecting for the bank must:

- **Identify themselves** with a bank or agency ID card. Agents also carry an authorisation letter and the bank's notice, both showing the agency's phone number and the bank's grievance officer.
- Discuss the dues **only with the borrower or guarantor**, civilly and with decency.
- Call or visit **only between 08:00 and 19:00**, unless the borrower asks otherwise, and honour requests to avoid certain times.
- Meet at the **borrower's chosen place**. Home or work is allowed only if no place is chosen or the borrower misses two or more meetings there.
- Avoid **bereavements, medical emergencies, weddings** and similar occasions.
- Send only bank-approved written messages, and **give a receipt** for every payment.

The bank must **log and record recovery calls**, tell borrowers they are recorded, and keep recordings for **six months** (longer if the matter is in court).

cards.title: Harsh or acceptable?
cards.prompt: Sort each recovery action under paragraph 454Z and the conduct rules.

items.text: A polite reminder call at 10:30 am, recorded after telling the borrower
Meeting the borrower at the café she chose, with an ID card and authorisation letter
Giving a receipt immediately for a cash part-payment
Posting the borrower's photo and loan details on social media
Telling the borrower's suppliers she is a defaulter
Twenty calls a day from different numbers
Saying the borrower will be arrested tomorrow if she does not pay
Calling at 9:40 pm without any request from the borrower

lines.text: Our partner wants us to finance smartphones and lock the phone on day one of default. It works, apparently.
And they want to read the borrower's contacts to find relatives who can pay.
From January, RBI allows device locking only for loans that financed that device, only gradually, and never using the borrower's personal data.
Get it wrong and the bank pays ₹250 an hour in compensation. Let's read the conditions carefully.

cards.title: Device locking for a financed phone
cards.caption: Paragraphs 454S-454U. Essential functions such as incoming calls, SMS and emergency SOS are never blocked.

items.label: Loan agreement
items.detail: Must expressly permit restrictions and set out the procedure; mechanism certified by the device maker or OS platform where available.

items.label: No restriction yet
items.detail: No restriction until the loan is 30 days past due and notices have gone unpaid.

items.label: Gradual restrictions
items.detail: Step-by-step, after notice; outgoing calls stay open.

items.label: Full restrictions
items.detail: Full set, including outgoing calls, only after 60 days past due.

items.label: Unlock
items.detail: Reverse restrictions within an hour of receiving the dues.

cards.title: The partner's lock-and-trace plan
cards.situation: A device-financing partner proposes: lock the whole phone on the first missed instalment, read the borrower's contact list to call relatives, and unlock 'by the next working day' after payment. Arjun wants to sign by December.

choices.text: Reject the plan; allow only gradual restrictions after 30 days past due, full ones after 60, no personal data access, and unlocking within one hour
choices.outcome: Correct. Paragraphs 454S-454U set those limits, protect essential functions and the borrower's work, and ban any use of contacts, SMS, photos or location data.

choices.text: Accept the lock but drop the contact-list access
choices.outcome: Better, but locking on the first missed instalment and unlocking the next day both breach the rules. Wrongful or late restrictions cost ₹250 an hour in compensation, capped at the loan amount.

choices.text: Accept it, since the partner runs the technology
choices.outcome: The bank stays responsible for its third-party service provider. Every element of this plan breaches the 2027 rules.

cards.title: Recovery rules and their numbers
cards.prompt: Match each 2027 recovery rule to its figure.

pairs.right: 08:00 to 19:00, unless the borrower asks otherwise
At least one day before the first in-person visit
Six months, or until a court case is disposed of
Within seven calendar days of a change
₹250 per hour, capped at the loan amount disbursed

cards.question: Sunita asked the agent to meet her at her shop, but she missed two arranged meetings there. Where may the agent now contact her?
options: Only at the branch, never elsewhere
At her residence or her place of business
At her supplier's office, to apply pressure
cards.explanation: Paragraph 454Y(5): contact is ordinarily at the borrower's chosen place; if she fails to appear there on two or more successive occasions, the agent may contact her at her residence or business.

cards.title: Real case: RBL Bank recovery findings (RBI, 2023)
cards.body:
**What RBI found.** The same 2023 order against RBL Bank (penalty about **₹2.27 crore**) found failures with recovery agents in the years under review. The bank had failed to:

- ensure its recovery agents did **not intimidate or harass** borrowers;
- ensure agents had completed the training course and obtained the **IIBF certificate** before onboarding;
- carry out **pre-employment police verification** of agents; and
- **inform borrowers of the recovery agency's details** when forwarding their cases.

**Why it matters.** Each failure maps onto a 2027 rule: IIBF certification (454I), antecedent verification (454H), prior notice to the borrower (454L) and the ban on harsh practices (454Z). The new rules make these duties more detailed, not lighter.

*Source: RBI press release 2022-2023/1891.*

cards.title: Put the grievance officer on every page
cards.body:
From 2027 every recovery communication must name the bank's **grievance redressal officer**, with name, email, phone and address. Also:

- Set up a **dedicated recovery grievance mechanism** and describe it in the loan agreement and the agency notice.
- Make sure **targets and incentives** for staff and agencies do not push agents toward harsh practices.
- Share borrower data with agencies **only as far as needed**, with penalties for misuse.
- Have a **compensation provision** in the recovery policy for losses caused by non-compliant recovery.

cards.title: Collections Room take-aways
items: Lending conduct rules sit in Chapter VIII of the Responsible Business Conduct Directions; use prescribed formats such as the KFS where RBI sets them.
Loan service providers and apps selling for the bank are DSAs under the 2027 sales rules, and their screens must avoid dark patterns.
From 1 January 2027 recovery agencies may use only IIBF-certified agents, after due diligence and a code of conduct undertaking.
Contact 08:00-19:00, notify agency details a day ahead, record calls for six months and never use harsh methods.
Device locks apply only to financed devices, gradually after 30 and 60 days past due, never using personal data, and must be lifted within one hour of payment.

cards.prompt: Imagine you are the borrower on the other end of a recovery call your bank makes. Which of the 2027 rules would matter most to you, and is your bank ready to prove it follows them?

quiz.question: From 1 January 2027, which agents may a recovery agency engaged by a commercial bank use?
options: Any agent with three years' collections experience
Agents certified by the bank's own training team
Any agent who signs the code of conduct
Only agents holding the IIBF certificate after its Debt Recovery Agents training
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 454I limits agencies to agents with the IIBF certificate earned through the Debt Recovery Agents programme of IIBF or an institute tied up with it.

quiz.question: Between what hours may a bank employee or recovery agent normally contact a borrower about overdue dues under the 2027 rules?
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 454Y(4) sets 08:00 to 19:00 for recovery contact, unless the borrower asks otherwise. The 09:00-19:00 window applies to sales calls under the Second Amendment.

quiz.question: Deccan Lotus Bank assigns Sunita's account to a recovery agency for a home visit. What must the bank do before the first visit?
options: Nothing, since the agent will carry an ID card
Publish her name on the defaulters list
Inform her guarantor's employer
Give her the agency's details at least one day before the first visit
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 454L requires the bank to send the recovery agency's details to the borrower or guarantor at least one day before the first in-person visit.

quiz.question: How long must a bank keep recordings of recovery calls under the 2027 rules?
options: Three months from the call
Six months from the call, or until a sub judice case is disposed of
One year after the loan is closed
Eight years, as for KYC records
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 454P requires call recordings to be kept for six months from the date of the call, or until disposal where the matter is sub judice.

quiz.question: Which act is listed as a harsh recovery practice in paragraph 454Z?
options: Sending a bank-approved reminder letter
Visiting at 11 am at the borrower's chosen place
Making false statements about what will happen if the borrower does not pay
Calling once a week during permitted hours
quiz.explanation: False or misleading representations about the debt or the consequences of non-payment are expressly harsh, along with abuse, threats, social media shaming and excessive calls.

quiz.question: A bank financed a borrower's laptop. When may it first start restricting the laptop's functions?
options: On the first day an instalment is missed
Only after the loan is 90 days past due
Whenever the loan agreement allows it
After the loan is 30 days past due and notices have gone unpaid
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 454S(3): no restriction until the loan is 30 days past due and unpaid despite notices; gradual restrictions after that, full restrictions only after 60 days past due.

quiz.question: A financed phone stays locked for five hours after the borrower clears her dues, because of the bank's error. What compensation applies?
options: A flat ₹500, whatever the delay
Nothing, if the phone is unlocked within one working day
₹250 per hour until it is remedied, capped at the loan amount disbursed
Only what the RBI Ombudsman later awards
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 454T(5)-(6): restrictions must be reversed within one hour of payment; for wrongful or delayed reversal the bank pays ₹250 per hour, capped at the loan amount disbursed.

quiz.question: A device-financing partner wants to use the borrower's contact list to trace relatives for repayment. What do the 2027 rules say?
options: It is allowed if the loan agreement says so
It is allowed after the loan is 60 days past due
It is allowed if only the borrower's spouse is called
Neither the bank nor its provider may access or use personal data on the device for any purpose
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 454U bans the bank and its provider from accessing or using personal data on the device, such as contacts, SMS, photos or location, for recovery or any other purpose.

quiz.question: A fintech app, contracted as a 'technology partner', markets Deccan Lotus Bank's personal loans to customers. How do the 2027 sales rules treat it?
options: As a DSA/DMA, so the bank's sales code, dark pattern ban and listing duties apply
As outside RBI's rules, since it is a technology partner
As a bank employee for all purposes
As a third-party product provider
quiz.explanation: The DSA/DMA definition covers any entity other than an employee engaged to sell or promote products, whatever the contract calls it, including loan service providers.

quiz.question: Which item must appear in every recovery-related communication from the bank from 2027?
options: The borrower's credit score
The recovery agent's commission rate
The names of the borrower's guarantors
The name, email, phone and address of the bank's grievance redressal officer
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 454AA requires all recovery communications to contain the name, email address, telephone number and address of the relevant grievance redressal officer.

sessions.title: Fraudulent Electronic Transactions, Oversight and Inspection Readiness
sessions.summary: Decide who bears the loss when fraudsters empty an account, using RBI's customer protection rules for electronic banking transactions from 1 January 2027, then pull the quest together: training duties, Board oversight, audit, records and what RBI inspectors look for.
objectives: Classify a fraudulent electronic banking transaction as bank negligence, customer negligence or third-party breach and decide liability
Apply the alert, reporting, acknowledgement, reversal and 45/60-day response rules
Explain the one-time small-value compensation for bona fide victims
Assemble the training, oversight, audit and record evidence RBI expects across complaints, sales, recovery and fraud

cards.title: ₹42,000 gone
cards.setting: Central Grievance Redress Cell, Mumbai. Monday, 8:50 am.

lines.text: (phone) Someone called pretending to be from the bank, sent me a link, and ₹42,000 left my account on Saturday night. I called your helpline at once.
We'll block further debits now and register this as a complaint. Please also report it to the National Cyber Crime Helpline, 1930.
Under the rules for transactions from January 2027, the burden of proving customer liability is on the bank, not on Sunita.
Final stage. Learn the liability rules, then get the bank ready for the RBI inspection team arriving in the new year.

cards.title: Who pays for a fraudulent transaction?

scenes.heading: The bank proves it
scenes.narration: For electronic banking transactions on or after the first of January 2027, the bank carries the burden of proving that the customer is liable.

scenes.heading: Bank at fault
scenes.narration: If the fraud happened because of the bank's negligence or deficiency, the customer has zero liability and gets the money back, whether or not she reported it.

scenes.heading: Somewhere else in the system
scenes.narration: If the weak point was a third party, such as a payment app or telecom provider, the customer has zero liability if she reports within five calendar days.

scenes.heading: Customer negligence
scenes.narration: If she shared her OTP or PIN, she bears the loss until she reports it. Anything after the report is the bank's loss.

scenes.heading: Answer on time
scenes.narration: The bank must examine the complaint, decide liability and respond within forty-five days for domestic frauds and sixty for cross-border ones.

items.label: Bank negligence, any time
items.detail: Zero liability and reversal, reported or not (76L).

items.label: Third-party breach, within 5 days
items.detail: Zero liability and reversal (76M).

items.label: Customer negligence, before report
items.detail: Customer bears the loss until reporting, less any small-value compensation (76N, 76T).

items.label: Third-party breach, after 5 days
items.detail: Liability as set in the bank's own policy (76M).

cards.question: Deccan Lotus Bank failed to send an SMS alert for a fraudulent UPI debit. The customer noticed it only after three weeks. What is her liability under the 2027 rules?
options: Her liability depends on the bank's policy because she reported late
Zero, because not sending mandatory alerts is bank negligence, whatever the reporting date
Full liability, because she did not check her account
cards.explanation: Not sending mandatory alerts is listed as bank negligence. Where the fraud is due to bank negligence, the customer has zero liability and a reversal, whether or not she reported it.

cards.title: What the bank must have in place
cards.body:
Paragraphs 76A-76J, for transactions on or after **1 January 2027**:

- A **published customer protection policy**: alert channels, customer rights and obligations, resolution timelines and awareness.
- Registered **mobile number** for electronic banking (except ATM cash withdrawals), verified at onboarding and at intervals the policy sets.
- **Instant SMS alerts** for every transaction above **₹500**, and **email alerts** where an email is registered. Alerts show account or card, amount, date, time, channel and beneficiary.
- **24x7 reporting** channels, a reply-to number in the SMS alert, and a direct link on the website and app home page.
- Each report is **registered as a complaint** with an immediate acknowledgement giving the complaint number, date and time.
- Prompt steps to **stop further unauthorised debits**, and advice to report on the **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal or 1930**.
- **No SMS charges** for alerts sent under regulation.

cards.title: Whose negligence?
cards.prompt: Sort each cause using the definitions in paragraphs 4(20B), 4(20C) and 4(26.1A).

items.text: The bank had no 24x7 channel to report a lost card
An internal fraud by a bank employee led to the debit
The customer gave his OTP to a caller posing as bank staff
The customer ignored the bank's specific warning that this payment looked like a scam
The customer kept his PIN written on the card
A payment gateway's systems were breached
A telecom provider issued a duplicate SIM to a fraudster

cards.title: Sunita's classification
cards.setting: Fraud operations, Navi Mumbai. Wednesday, 4:30 pm.

lines.text: The logs show Sunita entered her credentials on a fake link. That points to customer negligence, so she bears the loss up to her report.
Then check the small-value compensation. Her loss is under ₹50,000, she's an individual, and she reported to us and to 1930 the same night.
85 percent of ₹42,000 is ₹35,700, so the ₹25,000 cap applies. It's once in a lifetime, so we confirm she has never claimed before.
So I get ₹25,000 back, and more if the police recover the money?
Yes. If money is recovered, we recalculate on the net loss and pay you the difference.

cards.title: Responding to the fraud complaint
cards.situation: It is 2027. A customer, Mr D'Souza, reports a domestic fraudulent card-not-present transaction on his credit card. The investigation will take weeks, and the insurer has not yet responded. The fraud team proposes to tell him to wait for the insurance outcome before doing anything.

choices.text: Give a shadow reversal within five calendar days, investigate, and respond within 45 days of receiving the complaint
choices.outcome: Correct. For credit card frauds the bank must give a shadow reversal within five calendar days, and respond to domestic fraud complaints within 45 days, without waiting for insurance.

choices.text: Respond within 45 days, but reverse nothing until the insurer pays
choices.outcome: The timeline is right, but credit card frauds need a shadow reversal within five calendar days of notification, before investigation or insurance settlement ends.

choices.text: Wait for the insurer, then decide
choices.outcome: Insurance has no bearing on the customer's rights. Waiting risks breaching both the five-day shadow reversal and the 45-day response limit.

cards.title: Fraud liability rules by the numbers

items.label: Third-party breach report
items.detail: Calendar days for zero liability in third-party breach cases.

items.label: Domestic response limit
items.detail: To examine, establish liability and respond; 60 days for cross-border.

items.label: Small-value compensation
items.detail: Whichever is less, once in a lifetime, for losses up to ₹50,000.

items.label: SMS alert threshold
items.detail: Instant SMS for every electronic transaction above ₹500.

cards.title: Handling a fraud report, step by step
cards.prompt: Put the bank's steps for a reported fraudulent transaction in order.
steps: Register the report as a complaint and send an acknowledgement with the number, date and time
Stop further unauthorised debits and advise the customer to report to 1930 or the cyber crime portal
Classify the case: bank negligence, third-party breach or customer negligence
Reverse the transaction value-dated to the original date where the customer has zero liability
Respond within 45 days (domestic) or 60 days (cross-border), with reasons if liability is established

cards.title: Real cases: Union Bank and Central Bank (RBI, 2024 and 2026)
cards.body:
Both penalties concerned the **current rules on limiting customer liability**, which apply to transactions before 1 January 2027.

**Union Bank of India (March 2026, ₹95.40 lakh).** RBI found that the bank had not given a **shadow credit within 10 working days** of customers reporting unauthorised transactions, and had not given **24x7 access through multiple channels** to report them. A third charge concerned asset classification.

**Central Bank of India (June 2024, about ₹1.46 crore).** RBI found that in a few cases the bank had **not given the shadow credit within 10 working days**, and had not **resolved complaints and paid compensation within 90 days**. Another charge concerned a working capital loan.

**Lesson.** Reversal clocks and reporting channels are inspection targets. The 2027 rules tighten the clocks to 45 and 60 days for complaints and five calendar days for credit card shadow reversals.

*Sources: RBI press releases 2025-2026/2338 and 2024-2025/506.*

items.label: Analyse complaints
items.detail: The IO analyses complaint patterns every quarter and finds root causes.

items.label: Train frontline staff
items.detail: IO analysis feeds training on patterns, root causes and remedies (IO Directions 14(14)).

items.label: Certify sellers and agents
items.detail: Certificates before third-party sales postings; IIBF for recovery agents; train DSA sub-agents.

items.label: Check and audit
items.detail: Mystery shopping of card agents, annual IO audit, post-sale feedback, dark-pattern audits.

items.label: Report to the Board
items.detail: Customer Service Committee reviews IO reports, Ombudsman losses and fraud complaints.

cards.title: What the inspector will ask for
