cards.back: CMS showing three categories only, auto-escalation dates, IO reasoned decisions and replies within 30 days.
Appointment details sent to RBI within five working days, and quarterly reports by the 15th after each quarter.
Consent records kept until a year after the contract ends, staff certificates, DSA list and the code of conduct undertakings.
IIBF certificates, antecedent checks, published agency list, call logs and six months of recordings.
Alert and response timestamps, acknowledgements, classification and compensation records kept for audit.
Customer Service Committee minutes on IO reports, overruled decisions, Ombudsman outcomes and fraud complaints.

cards.question: Which is a training duty RBI has written into its Directions for commercial banks?
options: Annual refresher on the RB-IOS for every employee, set by the Scheme
Using the IO's complaint analysis in training for frontline staff
A national exam on fair practices for all branch managers
Mandatory IIBF certification for every bank employee
cards.explanation: Paragraph 14(14) of the IO Directions requires banks to use the analysis of IO-handled complaints in training and conferences for frontline staff. IIBF certification applies to recovery agents, not all staff.

cards.title: Inspection Room take-aways
items: For transactions from 1 January 2027 the bank must prove customer liability; bank negligence means zero liability whether or not the customer reported.
Third-party breaches give zero liability if reported within five calendar days; customer negligence leaves the loss with the customer until reporting.
Respond within 45 days (domestic) or 60 days (cross-border); credit card shadow reversals within five calendar days; reversals value-dated.
Bona fide individual victims with losses up to ₹50,000 may get 85% or ₹25,000, whichever is less, once in a lifetime.
Show evidence: complaint analysis in training, certificates, IIBF agents, records, audits and Customer Service Committee oversight.

cards.prompt: If an RBI inspector arrived tomorrow, which piece of evidence from this quest would your team find hardest to produce? Who would you ask to fix it, and by when?

quiz.question: For electronic banking transactions on or after 1 January 2027, who bears the burden of proving customer liability in a fraud complaint?
options: The bank
The customer
The beneficiary bank
The RBI Ombudsman
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 76K places the burden of proving customer liability in complaints about fraudulent electronic banking transactions on the bank.

quiz.question: A fraudulent debit resulted from a breach at a payment gateway. The customer reported it on the third day. What is her liability?
options: Up to the limit in the bank's policy
Full liability until the gateway pays
Half the loss, shared with the bank
Zero, with reversal, because she reported a third-party breach within five calendar days
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 76M: in a third-party breach reported within five calendar days, the customer has zero liability and the transaction is reversed. After five days the bank's policy decides.

quiz.question: Which is defined as negligence by a customer in the 2027 rules?
options: Not having a smartphone banking app
Ignoring a specific, clear warning from the bank that the payment is likely a scam
Reporting a fraud on the sixth day
Using a debit card for online shopping
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 4(20C) lists ignoring specific, directed and clear warnings as customer negligence, along with sharing credentials, late reporting, malicious apps and not updating contact details.

quiz.question: A customer shared his OTP with a fraudster at 10 pm and reported the fraud at 11 pm. A further debit occurred at 11:30 pm. Who bears the 11:30 pm loss?
options: The customer, as the original negligence was his
The beneficiary bank alone
Split equally between the customer and the bank
The bank, since losses after the customer's report fall on the bank
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 76O: loss from any unauthorised transaction after the customer reports the fraud is borne by the bank. The customer bears losses from his own negligence only until he reports.

quiz.question: What is the maximum time for a bank to examine, establish liability and respond to a complaint about a domestic fraudulent electronic transaction from 2027?
options: 45 calendar days from receipt of the complaint
30 calendar days from the transaction
90 days from receipt of the complaint
10 working days from notification
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 76Q sets a ceiling of 45 calendar days for domestic and 60 calendar days for cross-border frauds. The 10-working-day and 90-day figures belong to the pre-2027 rules.

quiz.question: For a credit card fraud complaint under the 2027 rules, within what time must the bank give a shadow reversal?
options: Within ten working days of the investigation ending
Within five calendar days of the customer's notification
Within 45 days, together with the final response
Only after the insurer settles the claim
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 76R requires a shadow reversal equal to the disputed amount within five calendar days of notification for credit card frauds.

quiz.question: Above what value must a bank send instant SMS alerts for every electronic banking transaction from 2027?
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 76D requires instant SMS alerts for all electronic transactions above ₹500. For smaller ones the bank may send SMS under its policy, without charge.

quiz.question: A bona fide individual victim of customer-negligence fraud lost ₹20,000 and reported it to the bank and 1930 within five days. No recovery is made. What compensation applies?
options: ₹25,000, the fixed compensation amount
₹17,000, which is 85 percent of the net loss
₹20,000, the full loss
Nothing, because the customer was negligent
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 76T: 85 percent of the net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is less, once in a lifetime, for losses up to ₹50,000. Here 85 percent of ₹20,000 is ₹17,000.

quiz.question: Under the IO Directions, how must Deccan Lotus Bank use the IO's analysis of complaints?
options: Only in the annual report to shareholders
In training and conferences for frontline staff on complaint patterns, root causes and remedies
To set individual sales targets
To decide which customers to decline
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 14(14) requires the bank to use the analysis of IO-handled complaints in training to raise frontline awareness of patterns, root causes and remedies, with the IO involved where needed.

quiz.question: What information on RBI Ombudsman outcomes must go to the Board's Customer Service Committee each quarter?
options: Only complaints where the bank won
The names of all complainants who filed
Complaints decided for complainants, with an analysis of at least the top five categories and remedies
Only complaints worth more than ₹30 lakh
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 13(5): complaints the RBI Ombudsman resolved for the complainant go to the Customer Service Committee quarterly, with an analysis of at least the top five categories and remedial measures.

regulators: RBI Ombudsman (Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026)
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Internal Ombudsman) Directions, 2026
references.provision: Paragraphs 3-16, incl. 14(1), 14(9), 14(12)-(14) (escalation, 30-day decision, RBI Ombudsman advice, staff training)
references.note: Banks with 10 or more outlets must appoint an Internal Ombudsman, auto-escalate partly resolved or rejected complaints for review, decide within 30 days, tell customers about the RBI Ombudsman, and use complaint analysis to train frontline staff.

references.title: Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026: Frequently Asked Questions
references.note: RBI's own explanation of the 2026 Scheme: coverage, filing channels, when a complaint can be filed, non-maintainable complaints, compensation limits, settlement, awards and appeals.

references.title: Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026
references.note: The Scheme itself, in force from 1 July 2026 and replacing the 2021 Scheme (announced in RBI press release of 16 January 2026). The PDF host blocks automated access, so the text was not opened; facts in this quest come from RBI's FAQ page.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
references.note: Consolidates RBI's customer service, grievance redress and responsible lending conduct instructions for commercial banks. Published only as a PDF on rbidocs.rbi.org.in, which blocks automated access, so it was not opened.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Second Amendment Directions, 2026
references.provision: New paragraphs 85A-85ZA and Annex IIA (effective 1 January 2027)
references.note: Defines mis-selling and compulsory bundling; requires a sales policy, explicit consent with a default of no, suitability checks, regulator-prescribed qualifications for sellers, a code of conduct, post-sale feedback, no dark patterns, and full refunds where mis-selling is established.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026
references.provision: New section DA, paragraphs 76A-76V (transactions on or after 1 January 2027)
references.note: Replaces the limited-liability rules for unauthorised electronic banking transactions: bank bears the burden of proof, zero liability for bank negligence and for third-party breaches reported within five calendar days, 45/60-day response limits, and a one-time small-value compensation scheme.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fourth Amendment Directions, 2026
references.provision: New Section L, paragraphs 454A-454AB, incl. 454I (IIBF certificate) and 454Z (harsh practices) (effective 1 January 2027)
references.note: Recovery conduct: a recovery policy, IIBF-certified agents only, a code of conduct, published agency lists, prior notice to borrowers, contact between 08:00 and 19:00, call recording, limits on device locking and a dedicated recovery grievance mechanism.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Miscellaneous) Directions, 2025
references.note: A certificate course is mandatory before staff are posted to marketing of third-party retail products and wealth management, among other areas, to curb mis-selling; certifications prescribed by other financial regulators must also be met.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Credit Cards and Debit Cards: Issuance and Conduct) Directions, 2025
references.note: Card issuers must check agents through random checks and mystery shopping, stop mis-selling of cards, train call-centre staff to handle and escalate complaints, and compensate customers for their own faults and delays.

references.title: Certification Programme for sale and/or distribution of mutual fund products (SEBI Circular Cir/IMD/DF/5/2010)
references.issuer: Securities and Exchange Board of India
references.note: Anyone selling or distributing mutual fund products must pass the NISM certification examination and keep it current through continuing professional education.

references.title: RBI press release: RBI issues Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026 (16 January 2026)
references.note: Announces the RB-IOS 2026, finalised after public feedback on the October 2025 draft, in force from 1 July 2026.

bank.question: A Deccan Lotus Bank branch rejects a complaint about a wrong locker charge. Under the IO Directions 2026, who may close the rejected complaint at branch level?
options: The branch manager, after recording reasons in the system
Nobody at that branch; it is reviewed at a fairly senior level and auto-escalated to the IO
The officer who handled it, if the customer agrees
The regional office, without IO involvement, if the charge is under ₹1,000
bank.explanation: Paragraph 14(4): a complaint may not be closed by the same branch or touch point. A rejection or partial resolution is reviewed at a fairly senior level and then goes to the IO.

bank.question: The bank's Customer Service Committee wants to replace the IO after 18 months because his decisions are 'too generous'. What do the Directions require?
options: The Competent Authority may remove the IO at any time without reasons
The IO may be removed only with RBI's prior approval
Removal before the contracted term needs the Customer Service Committee's approval, and IO terms are at least three years
Removal is allowed after one year if the IO has overruled the bank often
bank.explanation: The IO has a fixed term of at least three years. Removal before completion needs the Customer Service Committee's approval. Committees also review overruled decisions, so 'generous' decisions are not a removal ground.

bank.question: The IO resigns unexpectedly on 1 September. What must Deccan Lotus Bank do?
options: Inform RBI within 10 working days and appoint a new eligible IO within three months
Inform RBI within 30 days and appoint within six months
Leave the post vacant until the next Board meeting
Ask the head of retail banking to act as IO until a new one is found
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8(6): for a vacancy beyond the bank's control, inform RBI within 10 working days and appoint a new IO within three months. The post must never be vacant; the Deputy IO acts meanwhile.

bank.question: Both the IO and the Deputy IO are away for three weeks. What may the bank do?
options: Designate a serving GM-rank official as IO for up to one month, with Customer Service Committee approval and no reporting line to business
Suspend escalations until they return
Ask the Chief Compliance Officer to decide complaints under her own authority
Send all rejected complaints straight to the RBI Ombudsman
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8(3) allows, in rare cases, a serving GM-rank official to be designated as IO for up to one month with Committee approval, without reporting to business verticals during that period.

bank.question: What may the IO recommend beyond the compensation set by RBI rules or the bank's policy?
options: Compensation under the RB-IOS for consequential loss, lost time, expenses and harassment
Disciplinary action against named employees
A waiver of all the customer's future fees
Nothing; the IO cannot recommend compensation
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12(5) lets the IO recommend extra compensation in line with the RB-IOS for consequential loss, loss of time, expenses and harassment or mental agony.

bank.question: Which statement about the IO's access to RBI systems is correct?
options: The IO can file complaints on RBI's CMS for customers
The IO decides RBI Ombudsman cases about the bank
The IO has read-only access to RBI's Complaint Management System to follow Ombudsman and Appellate Authority decisions
The IO has no access to any RBI system
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12(8): the IO and Deputy IO have read-only access to RBI's CMS so they can keep up with decisions of the RBI Ombudsman and the Appellate Authority. The bank requests it from CEPD.

bank.question: How often must the IO analyse the pattern of complaints and report to the Customer Service Committee?
options: Analyse and report once a year
Analyse monthly; report only when asked
Analyse half-yearly; report annually
Analyse quarterly; report preferably quarterly and at least half-yearly
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12(6) requires quarterly analysis by product, category, customer group and location. Paragraph 13(2) requires reports to the Committee preferably quarterly but not less than half-yearly.

bank.question: When assessing the IO's performance, what must the Customer Service Committee also analyse?
options: Cases where the IO's decision differed substantially from the RBI Ombudsman's later decision
The amount of money the IO saved the bank
How many complaints the IO rejected
Customer satisfaction scores for the branches
bank.explanation: Paragraph 14(15): besides pendency and work towards uniform redress, the Committee analyses cases with a substantive difference between the IO's decision and the RBI Ombudsman's.

bank.question: Deccan Lotus Bank appointed a new Deputy IO on Monday. When must it send her details to RBI?
options: Within 30 days, with the quarterly report
Only at the next annual return
Within 10 working days, to the Department of Supervision
Within five working days, to RBI's Consumer Education and Protection Department
bank.explanation: Paragraph 16(1) requires details of a newly appointed IO or Deputy IO within five working days, to CEPD at RBI's Central Office.

bank.question: A customer complained to his bank on 20 June 2026, and the bank rejected it in July. Which Scheme governs a complaint he files with the RBI Ombudsman in August 2026?
options: RB-IOS 2021, since his first complaint to the bank was before 1 July
RB-IOS 2026, since his complaint to the RBI Ombudsman is received after 1 July 2026
Neither, as complaints from the changeover period are excluded
Whichever Scheme the customer prefers
bank.explanation: RBI's FAQ says complaints received before 1 July 2026 continue under RB-IOS 2021. A complaint received by the RBI Ombudsman in August 2026 falls under RB-IOS 2026.

bank.question: A card dispute falls under a card network rule giving the issuer 45 days to resolve it. When can the cardholder approach the RBI Ombudsman without any reply?
options: After 30 days, as the Scheme overrides network timelines
After 45 days, as the higher of 30 days and the network timeline applies
After 60 days in all card cases
Only after the network itself decides the dispute
bank.explanation: RBI's FAQ (Q17): a customer may file if there is no reply within 30 days or the time set by RBI, NPCI or card network guidelines, whichever is higher.

bank.question: Which complaint is maintainable under RB-IOS 2026?
options: A dispute between two banks over an interbank settlement
A bank employee's complaint about his transfer
A complaint by a vendor about an unpaid invoice from the bank
A complaint about a bank's failure to act on a stop-payment instruction, raised with the bank and rejected two weeks ago
bank.explanation: Disputes between regulated entities, employer-employee matters and vendor disputes are not maintainable. A customer's service complaint, raised first with the bank and rejected, may proceed.

bank.question: During the RBI Ombudsman's examination, the complainant files a civil suit on the same cause of action. What can happen?
options: The Ombudsman must wait for the court and then decide
The bank must settle at once
The RBI Ombudsman may reject the complaint at that stage
The complaint moves automatically to the Appellate Authority
bank.explanation: RBI's FAQ (Q26) lists a case on the same cause of action filed before a court, tribunal, arbitrator or other forum during the examination as a ground for rejection at any stage.

bank.question: A customer claims ₹80 lakh in consequential loss after a bank wrongly dishonoured a large cheque. What does RB-IOS 2026 allow?
options: The Ombudsman can award the full ₹80 lakh
Complaints above ₹30 lakh are not maintainable at all
The Ombudsman can award only ₹3 lakh in total
No limit on the disputed amount, but consequential loss compensation is capped at ₹30 lakh
bank.explanation: There is no limit on the amount in dispute, but compensation for consequential loss is capped at ₹30 lakh (plus up to ₹3 lakh for time, expenses and harassment). A claim beyond the Ombudsman's power can be a rejection ground.

bank.question: A bank wants to appeal an award passed because it failed to give the Ombudsman the documents requested. What does RB-IOS 2026 say?
options: The bank may appeal within 30 days with prior sanction
The bank may appeal within 60 days
The bank may appeal only if the customer agrees
No appeal lies for the bank against an award passed for its failure to furnish information
bank.explanation: RBI's FAQ (Q31): a regulated entity may appeal an award with prior sanction, but not one passed because it failed to furnish required information or documents.

bank.question: Under RBI's alternate grievance redress framework, what does the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre do?
options: Hears appeals against Ombudsman awards
Supervises banks' Internal Ombudsmen
Runs RBI's 24x7 IVRS contact line
Receives and processes email and physical complaints filed under the Scheme
bank.explanation: The CRPC in Chandigarh receives and processes complaints sent by email or post. Online complaints are registered on the CMS portal; appeals go to the Appellate Authority.

bank.question: A Hindi-speaking customer from Odisha wants to describe her complaint in Odia on the CMS portal. What does RBI's FAQ say?
options: She must translate it into Hindi or English
Only paper complaints are accepted in regional languages
She must use the Contact Centre to file in Odia
The portal works in Hindi and English, but the description may be typed in any language
bank.explanation: RBI's FAQ (Q37): CMS works in Hindi and English, and the facts may be entered in any language within the character limit. Email and paper complaints may be in any language.

bank.question: A customer took a loan in March 2027 and was charged for a loan protection policy funded from the loan, with no separate explicit consent. Which rule does this break?
options: The ban on funding any product from a loan without the customer's explicit consent
The ban on any insurance sold with loans
The 09:00-19:00 contact window
The rule that third-party products may only be sold online
bank.explanation: Paragraph 85W bars a bank from funding a customer's purchase of any product out of a loan without explicit consent. Insurance alongside a loan is not banned as such.

bank.question: Arjun proposes keeping signed consent forms for six months after each sale. What do the 2027 rules require?
options: Six months after the sale is enough
Keep consent records until one year after the contract for the product ends
Five years from the date of sale
Only until the free-look period expires
bank.explanation: Paragraph 85G requires the bank to preserve consent and related records until one year from the date the contractual agreement for the product ends.

bank.question: Deccan Lotus Bank adds a new DSA for credit card sales. What must it do with its public DSA list?
options: Nothing until the annual list update
Report it to RBI within 30 days instead
Update the website list, with type, address, period and products, within seven calendar days
Publish only the DSA's name, as the other details are confidential
bank.explanation: Paragraph 85C requires an up-to-date list of DSAs/DMAs on the website, showing type, address, period of engagement and products, updated within seven calendar days of any change.

bank.question: A customer complains of mis-selling of a bank fixed deposit product 25 days after receiving the signed terms. No other regulator's timeline applies. Is the complaint in time under the 2027 rules?
options: No, as mis-selling complaints must be made within 15 days
Yes, as there is no time limit for mis-selling
Yes, as the default window is 30 days from receiving the signed terms
No, as the window runs from the application date
bank.explanation: Paragraph 85Z: where the product's regulator sets no timeline, the customer can complain within 30 days of receiving the signed copy of the terms or agreement.

bank.question: Which practice breaks the 2027 rules for staff, DSAs and third-party representatives in a branch?
options: Telling the customer the fees and interest rate upfront
Calling a customer at 6 pm about a product she asked about
Visiting a customer's home without her explicit consent to follow up a lead
Giving the grievance officer's details when asked
bank.explanation: Paragraph 85N(8) bars visits to a customer's home, business or office without explicit consent. Upfront disclosure, calls within 09:00-19:00 and sharing grievance details are required conduct.

bank.question: Under paragraph 59 of the Miscellaneous Directions, which posting does NOT require a certificate course before the staff member starts?
options: Branch teller handling cash deposits
Treasury dealer
Credit appraisal officer
Wealth management relationship manager
bank.explanation: Paragraph 59 lists treasury operations, risk management, accounting, credit management and marketing of third-party retail products and wealth management. Cash teller roles are not listed.

bank.question: A new RM already holds a relevant diploma from a reputed university. How does paragraph 59 treat it?
options: It replaces every certification, including SEBI's
It has no value; only IBA-recognised courses count
It may be considered as certification, though certifications prescribed by other regulators must still be met for third-party sales
It counts only if RBI approves it individually
bank.explanation: The proviso lets relevant graduate, diploma and certificate courses from reputed universities count, but for third-party sales the certifications other financial regulators prescribe must still be complied with.

bank.question: An app shows a savings rate of 7 percent in large type, while the minimum-balance condition for that rate sits in small grey text deep in the terms. Which dark pattern is closest?
options: Bait and switch
Nagging
Basket sneaking
Subscription trap
bank.explanation: RBI's Annex IIA gives advertising a higher savings rate without stating the minimum balance requirement as an example of bait and switch.

bank.question: What must a bank do before selling a non-standard product to an individual customer, under paragraph 85P?
options: Obtain a guarantor's consent
Assess suitability and appropriateness against her age, income, financial literacy and risk tolerance
Get the IO's prior approval
Check only that she has enough balance to pay
bank.explanation: Paragraph 85P requires a suitability and appropriateness assessment, comparing product features, risk-return, horizon, complexity and fees with the customer's profile, unless the product is deemed suitable for all.

bank.question: Under the 2027 recovery rules, which items must the bank's collection and recovery policy cover?
options: Only the commission payable to agencies
Only the list of borrowers to be called each day
Triggers, an escalation matrix, a code of conduct, deceased borrowers and a framework for financial distress
Only the legal remedies under the SARFAESI Act
bank.explanation: Paragraph 454D lists triggers for recovery, graded actions under an escalation matrix, a code of conduct, recovery on a borrower's death and a structured framework for financial distress, among others.

bank.question: Deccan Lotus Bank ends its contract with a recovery agency mid-way through several cases. What must it do for the affected borrowers?
options: Nothing, as borrowers deal only with the bank
Ask the agency to tell the borrowers itself
Wait until the new agency's first visit
Notify them immediately so they stop dealing with that agency, and update the website list
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 454K and 454N: on termination the bank must immediately notify the borrowers concerned and promptly update its published list of recovery agencies.

bank.question: A recovery agent plans to visit a borrower on the day of a family funeral, as she is sure to be home. What do the 2027 rules say?
options: Allowed, if within 08:00-19:00
Agents must avoid occasions such as bereavements, medical emergencies and weddings
Allowed, if the agent carries ID
Allowed, if the loan is more than 90 days overdue
bank.explanation: Paragraph 454Y(6) requires employees and agents to avoid inappropriate occasions such as bereavement, medical emergencies, calamities and marriage functions.

bank.question: A microfinance borrower failed twice to come to the agreed central collection place. Where may field staff now collect?
options: Only at the branch
At her residence or place of work
At her relatives' homes
At any public place of the staff's choosing
bank.explanation: Paragraph 454Y(7): microfinance collection is at a mutually agreed designated place, but field staff may collect at the borrower's home or work if she fails to appear there on two or more successive occasions.

bank.question: Farhan wants to set agency fees purely as a percentage of amounts collected within seven days of assignment. What must he check under paragraph 454Q?
options: That the targets and incentives do not induce harsh recovery practices
That the fee is below an RBI-set cap
That the IO approves the fee schedule
That borrowers consent to the fee
bank.explanation: Paragraph 454Q requires recovery targets and incentive structures for staff and agencies not to induce the harsh practices listed in 454Z.

bank.question: Which function must stay available on a financed phone even under full restrictions?
options: Outgoing calls to any number
Incoming calls, SMS and emergency SOS features
Social media and messaging apps
Mobile banking for other lenders
bank.explanation: Paragraph 454T(2) bars restricting essential functions such as incoming calls, SMS and emergency SOS. Outgoing calls may be restricted only after 60 days past due.

bank.question: A borrower with a locked financed phone wants to prepay half the loan now. What do the 2027 rules say?
options: Prepayment is barred while restrictions apply
Only full prepayment is allowed
The borrower may prepay partly or fully at any stage
Prepayment is allowed only before 30 days past due
bank.explanation: Paragraph 454T(8) gives the borrower the right to prepay the loan, partly or fully, at any stage.

bank.question: Which RBI finding against RBL Bank in 2023 matches today's rule on notifying borrowers?
options: The bank sent agents to borrowers' weddings
The bank locked borrowers' financed phones
The bank published agents' names on social media
The bank failed to inform borrowers of the recovery agency's details when forwarding their cases
bank.explanation: RBI's 2023 press release found RBL Bank had not informed borrowers of agency details when forwarding cases. The 2027 rules require this at least one day before the first visit.

bank.question: A fraud occurred because a bank employee misused customer data. The customer reports it after 40 days. What is the customer's liability for transactions in 2027?
options: Zero, because internal fraud is bank negligence, whatever the reporting date
Decided by the bank's policy, since she reported after five days
Full, since she reported late
Limited to 15 percent of the loss
bank.explanation: Internal frauds leading to unauthorised transactions are bank negligence under 4(20B). Paragraph 76L then gives zero liability and reversal whether or not the customer reported.

bank.question: Where a bank must reverse a fraudulent transaction, how must the reversal be made?
options: Dated on the day the bank finishes its investigation
Paid as a goodwill credit with no interest adjustment
Credited only after a police report is filed
Value-dated to the original transaction date, so the customer loses no interest and pays no extra charges
bank.explanation: Paragraph 76R requires reversals to be value-dated to the original date, so the customer suffers no loss of interest and bears no extra interest or charges.

bank.question: A bank rejects a fraud complaint because it finds the customer liable. What must it tell the customer?
options: Only that the complaint is closed
The reason for the rejection, with any supporting details
Nothing more, as the burden lies on the customer
The fraudster's identity
bank.explanation: Paragraph 76S: where customer liability is established, the bank must disclose the reasons for rejection and any supporting details.

bank.question: A bona fide victim lost ₹40,000 through customer negligence and ₹15,000 was recovered before compensation. What compensation is payable under paragraph 76T?
options: ₹21,250, being 85 percent of the ₹25,000 net loss
₹25,000, as the cap applies
₹34,000, being 85 percent of ₹40,000
₹12,750, being 85 percent of ₹15,000
bank.explanation: Compensation is 85 percent of the net loss (gross loss less recoveries) or ₹25,000, whichever is less. Net loss is ₹25,000, so 85 percent is ₹21,250. RBI's own illustration uses these figures.

bank.question: Within what time must the customer's bank pay small-value fraud compensation after receiving the customer's application?
options: Within five calendar days of receiving the application
Within 45 days, with the complaint response
Within 30 days after the quarter ends
After RBI reimburses its share
bank.explanation: Paragraph 76T(5): the customer's bank compensates within five calendar days of receiving the application. The bank later claims reimbursement from RBI and the beneficiary bank quarterly.

bank.question: For how long is the small-value compensation mechanism in paragraph 76T available?
options: Permanently, with no end date
For losses on frauds occurring up to one year from the Directions' effective date
Only for frauds reported in 2026
Until RBI's fund is exhausted
bank.explanation: Paragraph 76U makes compensation payable for losses on fraudulent transactions occurring up to one year from the effective date, with records kept for two years after the mechanism closes.

bank.question: Which body must periodically review fraudulent electronic transactions reported by customers, the action taken and the compensation mechanism?
options: The Internal Ombudsman alone
The Board or a Board committee identified for the purpose
The branch managers' forum
The RBI Ombudsman
bank.explanation: Paragraph 76V requires periodic reporting of fraud complaints to the Board or an identified committee, which reviews them, the action taken and grievance and compensation functioning.

bank.question: An RBI inspector asks for proof that the bank meets the card Directions' complaint handling rules for its call centre. Which evidence fits best?
options: The IO's personal contact list
The bank's annual advertising budget
Training records for call-centre staff on handling and escalating complaints, plus automatic escalation logs
A list of recovery agencies
bank.explanation: Paragraph 84 of the card Directions requires call-centre staff to be adequately trained to handle and escalate complaints, automatic escalation of unresolved complaints, and complaint or docket numbers.
